desc:
Etsy shop reports on sales, fees and ads give you one clear picture of what your shop really earns. Ecom Swift LLC turns your stats and payment statements into a plain report with a short note on what each section means.

## What is an Etsy shop report?

An Etsy shop report is a single document that pulls together the numbers spread across your shop: orders, revenue, fees, ad spend, shipping costs, traffic and listing performance. Etsy shows these in several places, and few sellers have time to combine them.

Ecom Swift LLC downloads your own stats and statements, joins them up and writes the result in plain language. We use only the data in your shop, so nothing is estimated from outside sources.

## Why revenue alone can mislead

A good month of revenue feels like success. But revenue is what the buyer paid, and a lot leaves before you keep any of it: fees, ad spend, shipping labels, materials and refunds. A shop can grow its sales and still earn less than before if costs rise faster.

Without a report, you cannot tell which listings bring orders and which only bring views, or whether ads are paying for themselves. Decisions then rest on feelings and memory.

## How a report changes your decisions

A report works because it puts cause next to effect. When you see ad spend beside the orders it produced, you can tell whether ads are worth continuing. When you see traffic sources beside conversion rate, you can tell whether visitors from search behave differently from visitors from social links. When you see your slowest listings, you know where to improve photos, titles or prices.

Each section of our report ends with one sentence about what it means and one idea to try. That keeps it useful instead of a pile of charts. The report cannot promise outcomes, but it does remove guesswork from your next move.

## What a good shop report includes

- Revenue, Etsy fees and net result for the period.
- Top listings by orders and by revenue.
- Slowest listings, with views but few orders.
- Ad spend and the orders linked to it.
- Traffic sources and conversion rate.
- Shipping costs compared with what buyers paid.
- Two or three months side by side, in higher packages.
- A listing-level profit view when you supply your costs.
- A dashboard sheet you can reuse, as a PDF and a spreadsheet.

## What we do

You send us the exports and statements from your shop, or you invite us with limited permissions so we can download them ourselves. We clean the data and check that figures agree across sources. Then we write the report in sections, each with a short explanation.

Basic looks at a single month and ends with three recommended next steps. Standard compares two months and adds traffic and conversion detail, shipping cost review and a spreadsheet. Premium covers a quarter, adds a listing-level profit view, a reusable dashboard sheet and a review call so we can walk through the findings with you.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Compare the same period of different months or years.
- Look at net result, not only revenue.
- Add your real material costs for a true profit view.
- Pick one or two actions from the report and try them.
- Keep each report so you can see change over time.

**Avoid:**
- Judging a listing from a few days of data.
- Ignoring shipping costs when you check margins.
- Reading one strong month as a trend.
- Changing everything at once after a report.
- Setting a gift-season month next to a slow one as if they were equal.

## Who this service is for

It suits an owner preparing for a tax filing or a loan conversation who needs tidy numbers. It helps a seller who spends on ads and wants proof, and a shop considering a new product line that wants to see which existing items do best.

## What we need from you

Send your stats and statement exports for the months you want covered, or invite us as a manager with limited permissions. If you want profit per listing, add your material costs. We never need passwords, and your data is used only to build your report.
